subject: Feature pricing deep-dive and next steps
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Zhang <olivia@finedge.com>, Nate Price <nate.price@finedge.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Mar 2026 18:05:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: feature economics from today's discovery

Hi Olivia / Nate —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap of the items we covered and the data we need to build a concrete pricing proposal and unit-econ model: 

- Your current pilot/alpha expectation: ~50M tokens/month (avg) with 120k qps burst windows during business hours.
- Primary feature profile: multi-turn assistant-style flow; median session ~1.2k tokens, avg sessions per user ~10/mo (so ~12k tokens/MAU/mo).
- Procurement target for a committed tier: target list price range of $8–$12 per 1M tokens (you flagged $10 as the middle ground).
- Business KPIs you care about: CAC payback (target <= 6–9 months), gross margin after inference cost (> 60%), and predictable unit price for forecasting.

Action items we agreed on: 
1) Olivia/Nate: share a simple usage histogram (percentile message lengths, daily active usage, and sessions per MAU) and current CAC estimate (ballpark ok).
2) Redwood: deliver a short unit-econ workbook and a 50M-commit pricing proposal showing tiered pricing and projected $/feature calculations.
3) Schedule a follow-up to walk the workbook and procurement timeline — proposed window: week of Mar 29.

I attached a first-pass workbook and a placeholder proposal PDF with tiered pricing scenarios. In the workbook you’ll see a quick calculation that uses the numbers from today:
- Assumption: 12,000 tokens per MAU/month
- Example price point: $9 per 1M tokens -> per-token = $0.000009 -> cost per MAU = $0.000009 * 12,000 = $0.108/mo

I also included scenario outputs for different revenue-per-MAU assumptions (so your product and finance folks can plug in real numbers). If you want us to model quantization or alternate model variants (reducing inference cost), say which model family you expect to run and we’ll add that line.

Next step: if you can share the histogram + CAC estimate this week, we’ll update the workbook and send a short write-up that maps to payback scenarios.

Thanks — talk soon.

--
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123
From: Olivia Zhang <olivia@finedge.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: feature economics from today's discovery

Jonas, thanks for the recap and the fast turnaround. Attachments received. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

- The 50M token estimate is conservative for Q3 ramp; could be 30–70M depending on adoption. Peak qps we saw in the pilot was ~140k for short bursts, not sustained.
- Our current CAC (blended across channels) is roughly $120 per paying acquisition; target is payback within 6 months for this monetized feature.
- Product pricing is not finalized; finance is looking at $15–$25 ARPU uplift for the feature (per paying MAU) depending on tiering and bundling.

Please highlight the scenario that gets us to <=6 months payback with a realistic committed tier. Also, procurement asked for an example committed quote for 50M/month with SLA and pricing ladder.

I’m happy to join the follow-up week of Mar 29; prefer Wed or Thu mornings PT.

Olivia Zhang
Head of Product, FinEdge
olivia@finedge.com | +1 650-555-0199
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Zhang <olivia@finedge.com>, Nate Price <nate.price@finedge.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 11:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: feature economics from today's discovery

Thanks Olivia — noted on the variability (30–70M) and the CAC figure. I pushed an updated workbook that includes a small scenario table; summary below (all numbers are illustrative based on assumptions in the workbook):

Assumptions used: 12k tokens/MAU/mo (your session/session frequency), CAC $120, target committed volume = 50M tokens/mo

Scenario (revenue per MAU -> contribution -> payback months):
- $10 ARPU: contribution = 10 - 0.108 = 9.892 -> payback = 120 / 9.892 = ~12.1 months
- $15 ARPU: contribution = 15 - 0.108 = 14.892 -> payback = 120 / 14.892 = ~8.1 months
- $20 ARPU: contribution = 20 - 0.108 = 19.892 -> payback = 120 / 19.892 = ~6.0 months
- $25 ARPU: contribution = 25 - 0.108 = 24.892 -> payback = 120 / 24.892 = ~4.8 months

Takeaway: at the 50M committed tier and the example price point of $9/1M tokens, you hit ~6 months payback only if ARPU for the feature is ~ $20/MAU. If finance expects $15 ARPU, payback is closer to ~8 months.

What we can do from the Redwood side to help compress payback: 
- Reduce gross inference cost via a model-variant/quantization recommendation (we can model a 30–40% reduction in inference cost if you accept a 2–3 point quality delta on some prompts).
- Offer a stepped commitment discount to get to $8/1M at 50M committed and a launch credit (we typically do 1–2 months free credits for new enterprise commitments).
- Provide tooling for prefix caching and batching for high-volume endpoints which will materially lower effective tokens sent (we modeled a realistic 7% token-savings in the workbook for your traffic profile).

I attached the updated workbook and a lightweight 50M/month proposal. If you’re open, I’ll loop Finance/RevOps on our side (Marissa) to show committed pricing and an example SOW.

Proposed follow-up: Wed Mar 31, 9:30 AM PT — 30 minutes to walk the workbook and procurement asks. Does that work?

Best,
Jonas

Attachments: FinEdge_Redwood_UnitEcon_v1.xlsx, proposal_finedge_50M_2026-03-22.pdf
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: FinEdge - unit economics ask + proposed concessions (internal)

Marissa / Ben —

Looping you both after the external thread. Quick summary and asks: 

Summary: FinEdge is evaluating a paid feature with an initial committed tier target ~50M tokens/mo (could be 30–70M). Their CAC = $120; they want payback <= 6 months. Using their usage profile, inference cost per MAU (at $9/1M tokens) is ~$0.108/mo. To hit <=6 months payback they need ~ $20 ARPU for the feature, or we need to lower their effective inference cost or provide commercial concessions.

Proposed options to present: 
1) Commercial: 50M committed -> $8.00 / 1M tokens + 1 month credit on onboarding. This moves cost per MAU to ~$0.096 and improves payback proportionally.
2) Technical: model-variant + quantization plan that reduces inference cost by ~35% (we should confirm quality delta with Applied ML).
3) Hybrid: $8.50 /1M + 30% token-savings (caching/batching) + 1 month credit. This is the most defensible without a large list-price hit.

Ask: can you run a quick margin check and put suggested committed pricing into the attached proposal PDF? Also need a call with RevOps to confirm billing terms and SLA language — Ben, can you own procurement thread and draft a sample SOW?

I’ll coordinate the customer follow-up for Wed Mar 31 9:30 AM PT if you confirm availability.

Thanks,
Jonas

--
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
